items.title: Household Products Stocks Q2 Recap: Benchmarking Clorox (NYSE:CLX)
items.summary: This article reviews the Q2 earnings season for the household products industry, highlighting the performances of key companies like Clorox, Spectrum Brands, Energizer, Procter & Gamble, and Reynolds. It notes that while revenues generally beat estimates, stock prices have seen a decline. The piece also briefly touches on broader market concerns, including AI and geopolitical events.

items.title: Why Is Ollie's Bargain Outlet (OLLI) Up 19.3% Since Last Earnings Report?
items.summary: Ollie's Bargain Outlet (OLLI) shares have risen 19.3% since its last earnings report, outperforming the S&P 500. The company reported better-than-expected Q2 fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings, driven by tariff refunds, despite a sales miss and declining comparable-store sales. While sales outlook was lowered, the profit guide was raised, reflecting mixed consumer trends and strategic initiatives like share buybacks and store expansion.

items.title: UBS cuts target for Cummins stock from USD 835.00 to USD 741.00
items.summary: UBS has lowered its price target for Cummins stock from USD 835.00 to USD 741.00, while maintaining a Buy rating, due to uncertainties surrounding EPA 2027 rules, inflation, and fuel costs. Despite the reduced target, Cummins recently signed a 1 gigawatt fleet deal and reported a 9% increase in Q2 2026 revenue to USD 9.46 billion, with diluted EPS at USD 6.73. The company also raised its full-year 2026 revenue-growth outlook.

items.title: Nucor-Yamato, Gerdau Increase Structural Steel Prices by $50/ton - News and Statistics
items.summary: Nucor-Yamato Steel and Gerdau Long Steel North America have both announced a $50 per short tonne price increase on various beams, piles, and other structural steel products, effective for orders placed on or after October 1st. This move follows Nucor's recent weekly increases in hot-rolled coil prices. Both companies stated they would continue to monitor market conditions to maintain competitiveness.

items.title: The Friday Checkout: Has Costco become grocery’s biggest threat?
items.summary: Costco is emerging as a significant threat to traditional grocers, demonstrating strong market share gains and sales growth in key departments like fresh food. The club retailer's recent financial results and consumer preference data indicate its increasing competitive edge, despite requiring a paid membership. This rise signals a need for traditional grocery stores to re-evaluate their strategies as Costco expands its influence.

items.title: We Energies plans new natural gas plant as data centers drive demand
items.summary: We Energies is proposing to construct a new 750-megawatt natural gas-fired power plant in Wrightstown, Outagamie County, in Wisconsin's Fox Valley. This initiative is being driven by the increasing energy demands from data centers. The planned facility would be located at the site of the existing Fox Energy Center.

items.title: Analog Devices Inc Stock (ADI) Moved Up by 3.22% on Oct 2: A Full Analysis
items.summary: Analog Devices Inc (ADI) stock increased by 3.22% on October 2, driven by its acquisition of Alif Semiconductor to address edge AI workloads and strong demand in industrial and hyperscaler markets. The company's strategic positioning in AI infrastructure and disciplined pricing are contributing to gross margin expansion and investor confidence. Technical indicators show buy signals, though one suggests an overbought condition, while fundamental analysis highlights solid revenue and net profit within the Technology Equipment industry.

items.title: U.S. Ford Motor Company Sales Up Two Percent In September 2026
items.summary: Ford Motor Company announced a two percent increase in U.S. sales for September 2026, totaling 169,132 units, with sales rising for the Ford brand but decreasing for Lincoln. Key performers included the Ford F-Series, Bronco, and Explorer, contributing to Ford's strong presence in the truck and large three-row SUV segments. Despite some model-specific decreases, the company remains on track with its full-year adjusted EBIT guidance.

items.title: JPMorgan cuts Zions Bancorp stock target to USD 65.00
items.summary: JPMorgan has lowered its price target for Zions Bancorporation (NASDAQ: ZION) from USD 75.00 to USD 65.00, while maintaining an underweight rating, which is below the broader consensus of USD 72.35. This comes despite Zions Bancorp reporting strong second-quarter revenues of USD 1.48 billion, an increase of 19.35% year-over-year, and net profit soaring by 85.66% to USD 453.00 million. The company's third-quarter results are anticipated on October 19, 2026.

items.title: PepsiCo recovery lags, but valuation remains attractive to UBS
items.summary: UBS maintains a "buy" rating on PepsiCo (NASDAQ:PEP) despite a slow North American recovery, citing attractive medium-term risk and reward in its valuation. The broker forecasts third-quarter earnings below consensus and expects the company to reiterate its full-year guidance, pointing to the low end due to weaker US sales and rising costs. While acknowledging investor concerns about strategic direction, UBS views PepsiCo's retreat from price investments favorably, expecting a regional turnaround to take time.
